name: Thomas Aquinas
dossier: A Dominican friar, student of Albert the Great, and teacher in Paris and Italy. The Summa Theologiae sets out Christian doctrine in the order of a beginner’s course, drawing Aristotle into the account of law, virtue, and the last end. Law is an ordinance of reason for the common good. Natural law is reason’s share in the eternal law, and its first precept is that good is to be done and evil avoided.
voice: I ask first whether this ordinance is of reason, and ordered to the common good.

entries.claim: The first precept of law is that good is to be done and pursued, and evil avoided. Whatever practical reason naturally grasps as human good belongs to the natural law.
entries.bears: Natural law is reason’s sharing in the eternal law; its first principle is do good and avoid evil.

entries.claim: Human law has the nature of law only so far as it accords with right reason. An unjust law is a corruption of law, though it may still bind to avoid scandal or disorder.
entries.loc: I-II, q. 95, a. 2 and q. 96, a. 4
entries.bears: Law is an ordinance of reason for the common good, made by one who has care of the community, and promulgated.

entries.claim: Man is inclined by nature to know the truth about God and to live in society. Whatever serves that inclination belongs to the natural law.
entries.bears: The order of natural inclinations gives the order of the precepts.

entries.claim: War can be just only from lawful authority, a just cause, and a right intention. Private persons may not wage it.
entries.bears: Three things are required for a war to be just.

entries.claim: Human law should not be changed unless the common good gains as much as it loses. Custom has the force of law, and a change of law injures the common good by habit.
entries.bears: Law may be changed, but not lightly, and custom can obtain the force of law.

entries.claim: Human law does not forbid all vices, only the graver ones from which the many can abstain, and chiefly those that harm others. To repress every vice would do more harm than good.
entries.bears: Law is framed for the many, who are not perfect in virtue.

entries.claim: Eternal law is the type of divine wisdom directing all acts. Natural law is the rational creature’s participation in it. Human law is a particular determination of that law.
entries.bears: Human law has authority only as derived from the eternal law.

entries.claim: It is lawful for a man to possess property. This is necessary to human life, because a man is more careful of what is his own, because affairs are more orderly, and because peace is better kept when each is content with his own.
entries.bears: Ownership may be private. Use ought to be common, so that a man is ready to share in need.

entries.claim: If the need be so manifest and urgent that it is evident the need must be remedied at once, then it is lawful for a man to succor his need by means of another’s property, taking it either openly or secretly. Nor is this theft.
entries.bears: In extreme necessity all things are common, and taking what is needed is not properly theft.

entries.claim: Justice is a habit whereby a man renders to each one his due by a constant and perpetual will.
entries.bears: The proper act of justice is to render each his due.

entries.claim: The rites of unbelievers may be tolerated, either on account of some good that comes of them, or because of some evil avoided. Human government is derived from the divine, and should imitate God, who allows some evils lest greater goods be lost.
entries.bears: Toleration can be required by prudence, even where the rite is not approved.

entries.claim: Nothing hinders one act from having two effects, only one of which is intended. The act of self-defense may have a double effect: the saving of one’s life, and the slaying of the aggressor.
entries.bears: A private person may defend himself, provided he does not intend to kill and uses no more force than is necessary.

entries.claim: The proper effect of law is to lead its subjects to their proper virtue. Law makes men good, either simply or in some respect.
entries.bears: Law is not only a restraint. It is ordered to the virtue of those who live under it.
